candidate.rationale: open_invariant_end merely restores/consumes ghost invariant state (consuming an InvariantBlockGuard and re-establishing the invariant). The necessary predicates that describe 'invariant is closed' or consumption of the guard are internal to the invariant/VIR machinery and not exposed as public vstd spec vocabulary, so any nontrivial postcondition would rely on private/internal predicates and risk being unsound. No meaningful, sound, non-vacuous public ensures can be expressed here.
risks: Proposing a postcondition that talks about 'closing' or 'restoring' the invariant would require internal predicates (e.g., 'invariant_closed' or ownership of the invariant ghost resource) which are not part of the public vstd API and could be unsound if used.
Specifying something weaker (like that some value equals input) would be vacuous or irrelevant to the function's purpose.
If later the public API is extended to expose appropriate predicates, this decision should be revisited to add a precise ensures clause.

candidate.rationale: Determinism-check feedback shows there is no candidate postcondition and no modeled observable output (semantic_disposition: compiler_internal). open_invariant_end only manipulates ghost/invariant machinery (consumes an InvariantBlockGuard and restores internal invariant state) and exposes no public vstd predicates describing that state. Any nontrivial ensures would either be vacuous or rely on verifier-internal ghost predicates (unsound to publish). Therefore no meaningful, sound public postcondition can be added now.
risks: Proposing a postcondition that asserts the invariant was 'closed' or that ownership of an invariant ghost resource was transferred would require internal predicates not part of the public vstd API and could be unsound.
Adding a trivial ensures (e.g., unit return or value-equality) would be vacuous and not helpful for verification or readability.
Publishing a spec that references compiler/internal semantics may mislead users and verification tooling; revisit if the public API later exposes safe predicates for invariant state.
